Abu Bakra turned back Al-Ahnaf, citing the Prophet: when two Muslims meet with swords, killer and killed both go to the Fire, for the killed also meant to kill.
Abusing a Muslim is evil-doing and killing him is disbelief.
Whoever kills a person who has a treaty with the Muslims will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, though it can be perceived from forty years' distance.
Ibn Abbas said the verse giving Hell to whoever kills a believer intentionally was never abrogated; another verse came after Muslims killed a man who greeted them with peace.
Ibn Abbas holds that verse 4.93 on deliberately killing a believer was never cancelled and allows no repentance, while verses 25.68-70, with their repentance, concerned the pagans.
A believer remains at liberty in his religion unless he kills unlawfully, bloodshed is the first case judged, and Al-Miqdad was told not to kill a foe who declared Islam.
The Prophet warned, also at the Farewell Hajj, that after him they must not turn disbelievers by striking one another's necks.
Usama was rebuked for killing a man who said none is worshipped but Allah; the pledge forbade killing, and two Muslims fighting with swords are both in the Fire.
Whoever kills a person under the Muslims' pledge of protection will not smell Paradise's fragrance, though it reaches across forty years' travel.
Whoever takes up arms against Muslims is not of them; do not point weapons or carry bare arrowheads, for Muslim blood is sacred and killing one another is disbelief.
